newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police see drop in crime.
newsitem.headline: S.African police see drop in crime.

text.p: South African police on Friday reported "a marked decrease" in serious crime in densely populated Gauteng province, which includes Johannesburg and Pretoria.
"Since the launch of the 'sword and shield' police plan in June, police in Gauteng have achieved tremendous successes," a statement said.
It said that for the four months since June, car hijackings were 28 percent down on the same period last year and armed robberies were down 20 percent.
"Generally, the crime rate in Gauteng has decreased 11.6 percent in the period of four months," the statement said, adding that 4,000 suspects in serious crimes had been arrested.
South Africa's wave of violent crime is cited as a factor in persuading skilled whites to emigrate and in scaring off foreign investors and tourists.
